messages:
Elena (support): Heads up — ACME Payments reported a sudden p95/p99 jump on their /v1/generate route around 09:12 UTC. They say errors are low but tails are terrible, requests timing out at 10s. They mentioned we rolled a continuous-batcher default yesterday. Can we triage?
Alex Chen: thanks, assigning. do we have customer id and route?
Elena (support): tenant=acme-pay, route=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2. They sent a sample request and latency graphs — p50 fine, p95 ~400ms -> p99 ~7.2s since ~09:12.
Maria Gomez: grabbing traces/grafana now. any recent deploys to batcher? @jin any config changes?
Jin Park: I did a config push to change global continuous-batcher defaults last night to reduce small-batch overhead (reduce hold_ms from 20->8). That was intended to lower avg latency but could increase tail if arrival spikes. I didn't target per-route overrides.
Alex Chen: that aligns with timeline. Elena, can you upload the customer sample payload or give us a trace id?
Elena (support): pasted sample payload and trace id: trace=tx-abc123. They said repro happens when they burst many small requests.
deploy-bot: Deployed config: continuous-batcher v2.1 -> changed default hold_ms=8, max_batch_size=32, batching_mode=continuous at 2026-03-15T02:00:12Z.
Chris R: quick summary of what might be happening: lowering hold_ms reduces average wait but makes batches smaller under bursty arrival patterns leading to more frequent tiny batches which can inflate p99 due to scheduling overhead and poor GPU utilization.
Maria Gomez: got grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/batching?orgId=1&var-route=/v1/generate&from=-1h to=now. I'm seeing pending_queue length spikes aligning with p99 spikes, and batch size distribution shifted to a lot of 1-3 item batches after the change.
Jin Park: interesting — small batches plus a background auto-scale thrash could add queueing. check kernel queueing on those boxes.
Alex Chen: steps to repro locally? we can stress test with many concurrent tiny requests.
Jin Park: repro steps I used: 1) set a dev route to continuous mode with hold_ms=8, max_batch_size=32. 2) run 200 clients sending 1-token prompts at random intervals (Poisson with mean 10 rps total). 3) measure tail latency and batch size distribution. I can share a small load script.
Alex Chen: please paste the script here.
Jin Park: ```bash
# tiny-burst repro
for i in {1..200}; do
  (while true; do
    curl -sS -X POST https://dev.redwood.local/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}' >/dev/null
    sleep $(awk -v min=0 -v max=0.1 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}')
  done) &
done
sleep 60
pkill -P $$
```
Jin Park: With that, I see many tiny batches and p99 ~6-8s.
Elena (support): ACME can also reproduce with a simple loop from their side. They said this started immediately after your default change.
Maria Gomez: logs show batcher hold timer firing rapidly and immediate batch flushes with sizes 1-3. Those batches then hit runtime scheduling gaps. Also see increased context-switches on GPU host nodes.
Chris R: mitigation plan options: 1) rollback global default immediately to previous hold_ms=20 2) set per-route override for acme-pay to hold_ms=20 or enable size-floor: min_batch_size=8 or adaptive batching 3) add a short jitter to batcher timers to reduce synchronized flushes.
Alex Chen: what's the fastest low-risk action?
Jin Park: per-route override is quick and surgical. I can push an override for tenant=acme-pay to hold_ms=20 and min_batch_size=4 in config service. That should reduce tiny batches and pull p99 down.
Maria Gomez: while Jin does that, I'll create a canary rule to detect tiny-batch frequency rising across tenants.
Alex Chen: Elena, ask ACME to keep traffic steady for 15 mins while we test; also request a fresh trace after we apply override.
Elena (support): on it, pinged them and they confirmed they'll keep sample traffic for 20m.
Jin Park: applying per-route override now. patch: ```yaml
routes:
  - tenant: acme-pay
    route: /v1/generate
    batcher:
      hold_ms: 20
      min_batch_size: 4
```
Jin Park: override pushed and rolled to 3 nodes (rollout id rot-778).
deploy-bot: Rollout rot-778 for per-route batching override started at 2026-03-15T09:46:02Z.
Maria Gomez: grafana shows batch size distribution shifting up; pending queue drops. p99 for acme route falling from ~7.2s -> ~420ms within 2 minutes. :thumbsup:
Elena (support): ACME confirms p99 looks back to normal and timeouts stopped. They asked why default change impacted them specifically.
Chris R: probable cause: ACME traffic pattern is many small independent requests with bursts; the global reduction of hold_ms optimized for average latency for steady workloads but harmed bursty tenants. Next steps: 1) revert global default to previous or make new global default more conservative 2) add per-tenant rollout guidelines for batcher changes 3) add an automated safety: when tiny-batch fraction > X% and p99 rises > Y, auto-increase hold_ms for that route 4) run a regression test that simulates small-burst traffic during config changes.
Alex Chen: agreed. Jin, please prepare a PR to revert global default back to hold_ms=20 and add an opt-in experimental faster default with an explicit tenant risk note. Also add a small E2E test for bursty small requests.
Jin Park: will do. PR draft link: https://git.redwood/infer/batcher-config/pull/342
Maria Gomez: I'll add dashboard alerts and a synthetic that sends Poisson tiny requests per route to catch this earlier.
Elena (support): ACME is happy with the mitigation. They want a short summary for the support ticket.
Alex Chen: Elena, send them: we applied a per-route batcher override to increase hold_ms and min_batch_size; this reduced tiny batches and fixed tail latency. We're rolling back the global default and adding improved guards + tests. Apologize for the disruption.
Elena (support): will send and close after customer ack.
Chris R: follow-ups: schedule a postmortem if this recurs; add a note in runbook about small-burst tenants and batching defaults.
Alex Chen: good job all. Jin, tag me on PR and include the E2E script.
Jin Park: done, thanks.
Maria Gomez: adding alert rules now.
Elena (support): ACME ack'd and closed. :white_check_mark:
